cells.tense: Right now, with the pen in hand, the refining attention is steady and present.
cells.act: keep building the thing with sustained craft
cells.ask: Give the piece you're making the same careful hour tomorrow, and let a single day of building be enough.
cells.core: You can tell the true line from the false one, and the whole pattern holds steady in your hands while you work. What you're building gets treated with the same care as everything you take apart and look at closely: you stay with the material until it shows you what it is. Some projects have a long arc in them, and the attention you spend now is what makes each day's piece fit the last. Whoever watches you work can't name what you're doing, but they can see you doing it, and that steadiness is the work. It's a good place to be standing, and it rarely announces itself.
cells.sheetLine: The small differences are yours to see, and you use them.
cells.verb: distinguishing the true line from the false one through patient attention
cells.place: a vantage point on the whole pattern, holding it steady while still standing inside it

cells.tense: Bracing for a future that can't be written in yet, the refining attention has been pulled past the work.
cells.act: do the giving in the open this time, where it was always done unseen
cells.ask: Show someone a piece of what you're making, or say plainly what it has cost, and leave the explaining at that.
cells.core: You're refining faster than the work can hold, ruling out the small wrong things before the pattern has had time to be whole. The habit of looking ahead is doing its job too well: every distinction gets made in advance, so the material doesn't get to surprise you, and the refining feeds the worry about whether it will hold. What you've already given up to get the distinctions right is sitting unseen, and the work undoes itself from the pressure of being watched before it exists. Let one finished piece stand where it can be seen. Claiming it isn't a presentation — just the thing you made being the thing you made.
cells.sheetLine: You're refining faster than the work can hold, and it shows.

cells.tense: Still standing at a door already behind you, the refining attention stopped arriving with the work.
cells.act: accept what is offered for what you gave
cells.ask: When someone close to you offers something for what you've already given, take it at its full size and stop there.
cells.core: You can still see clearly, but it isn't reaching the work anymore. Distinctions get made in private and stay private, and the pattern you'd normally catch goes past without your notice, because some of you is still at a door that closed. From the outside it looks like patience. From where you sit, it looks like nothing is arriving. That face of it comes back through exchange: what you've given gets an answer, and the answer counts. Take the next thing offered to you at its true size, and then the exchange is done. The doorway out is someone else's hand, held open.

cells.tense: In the present, the pen is down in a room where the writing is already done.
cells.act: let the satisfaction of a finished thing land
cells.ask: Use a finished piece of your work for an hour exactly as it is, and change nothing about it.
cells.core: You're making the distinctions and catching the whole pattern, and you'd say it was just following where it went. The work is getting finished, and the finished thing has its own standing — but somewhere along the way you stopped counting as the one who did it, and you read your own care as the situation being easy that time. What's left when the ink dries is exactly the part you keep skipping. Find a piece you already made and call it done. Not in your head — in your hands, used, appreciated, left exactly as it is. That's where careful attention and finishing meet.
cells.sheetLine: It's finished, you made it, and you don't have to say so.
cells.verb: distinguishing the true line from the false one through patient attention
